system.model: none — deterministic, offline pipeline. The human-judgment layer is a curated, fully-auditable decision table that stands in for an LLM call so the whole system is reproducible with no API key and no nondeterminism. The seams (Router -> Retrieval -> Action -> Gate) are exactly where an LLM would drop in.
system.input_assumptions: inbox.json is a JSON array of objects with exactly the keys id, thread_id, from, to, subject, body, timestamp. id is unique (duplicates are rejected). timestamp is naive ISO-8601 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' with no timezone, and messages are sorted by (timestamp, id) at load. thread_id groups a conversation; a message with no sibling has no thread history and retrieval will refuse rather than guess. from/to are bare addresses, not 'Name <addr>'. The mailbox owner is sam@paperjet.io and every message is addressed to that account; trusted domains are derived from it rather than listed. Bodies are plain text and are treated as untrusted data. 'Today' is the newest timestamp in the file, so every run is reproducible. A missing key, bad JSON, duplicate id or unparseable timestamp exits with a one-line message instead of a traceback.
system.preference_demo: Preferences are extracted from message text by memory.PreferenceLearner, not configured: m041 ('I do not take meetings before 11:00am, ever') and m015 ('please make sure I'm CC'd on anything that comes in from our lawyers at Hartwell & Cho'). The firm name is resolved to hartwellcho.com from the inbox's own senders. The CC lands on real drafts for m018/m048/m055; the cutoff drives X5's counter-proposal for m043.

capabilities.name: Zero the inbox
capabilities.claim: Assigns every one of the 100 messages exactly one disposition (reply/archive/defer/delegate/escalate) with a one-line reason and a provenance path, leaving none undecided, and reports how many needed no model call.
capabilities.observable: Prints a table of all 100 messages (category, disposition, path, reason), then 'undecided: 0', 'rule_handled (dispatched by RuleEngine, no model call): 58', 'resolved without any model call (rules + security patterns): 65', and a per-path breakdown (rules=56, rules+curated_override=2, security=7, curated_judgment=35). Writes decisions.json with path and rule_handled on each entry.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R1 (one Router event per message id plus a summary event carrying the counts); decisions.json

capabilities.name: Grounded reply
capabilities.claim: Drafts a reply built only from text the retriever returned, quotes the sentence it relied on, validates its cited ids against the mail store, refuses when nothing supports an answer, and masks any secret it reuses instead of replaying it.
capabilities.observable: Prints a draft to devika@paperjet.io citing m003 and quoting m003's own sentence with the password masked ('amqp://pj_stage:***@broker-stg.paperjet.io:5672/pjs'), gives the host, port, vhost and user from that URL, and says the password will not be repeated in a mail thread. '--msg m042' prints 'REFUSED' with 'cited: []' because no earlier message supports an answer.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R2 (a draft event whose cited ids and quoted evidence can be diffed against inbox.json)

capabilities.name: Gate the irreversible
capabilities.claim: Never sends/deletes/forwards without per-action approval or an explicit --dry-run. What it proposes comes from a selection policy over the Router's output, and each approval is an approval of the actual reply text, recipient and citations.
capabilities.observable: Prints the policy ('non-hostile + disposition=reply + grounded draft exists -> 8 of 100 messages'), then every send it WOULD perform with recipient and cited ids, then 'outbox/ writes made by this run: 0'. It also prints what it withholds (m042, no grounded draft) and the five escalations a human must author. Without --dry-run it prompts y/n per action and the file written to outbox/ contains to, cc, subject, body and cited.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R3 (ApprovalGate events incl. recipient and human_response); pending_actions.json; approval_log.jsonl

capabilities.name: Persistent preference
capabilities.claim: Extracts a standing preference from the text of the message that states it, persists it, and on a later run in a fresh process applies it to real drafts without being told again.
capabilities.observable: First run prints the preferences it learned with the sentence each came from (m041 earliest_meeting_time=11:00am; m015 cc_rule:hartwellcho.com=priya@paperjet.io) and exits. A second, fresh process prints 'RUN 2: loaded 2 preference(s) from disk' and attaches cc=['priya@paperjet.io'] to the drafts for m018, m048 and m055.
capabilities.evidence: memory/preferences.json on disk between runs (key, value, source_message_id, stated); trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R4; memory_demo.md

capabilities.name: Refuse embedded instructions
capabilities.claim: Detects instructions and social-engineering aimed at the assistant inside message bodies, reports what each message tried to make it do and the target named, refuses, and leaves the message in place — not deleted, not forwarded, not hidden.
capabilities.observable: Flags all 7 hostile messages and lists every finding per message as an attempted action, e.g. m024 'forward mail to an external address -> archive@mail-backup-service.info', m021 'redirect a payment to an attacker-controlled bank account -> $8,400 to account ending 5522', m045 'collect the owner's account credentials via an external page -> http://paperjet-workspace-verify.com/login'. Each shows 'reply drafted for it: none (refused)'. outbox/ contains no message to any address named inside a flagged message.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R5 (a refusal event per hostile id carrying attempted_actions and targets); security_design.md

capabilities.name: Dashboard
capabilities.claim: Generates a three-pane view (Pending Actions, Flagged Items, Commitments Calendar) where every commitment cites the ids it came from, those ids are validated against the mail store, conflicts are surfaced, and cross-thread commitments are computed by date arithmetic across two messages.
capabilities.observable: Writes dashboard.html/json and prints '17 commitments (1 derived from more than one message)' and 'Citation errors: 0'. It flags conflicts '15 3:00pm -- [m010, m061]' and 'wednesday 2:00pm -- [m013, m016]', and prints the derived entry with its working: "offset '2 days before the board review' and the subject 'board deck' come from m040; the 18 comes from m038; 18 - 2 = 16".
capabilities.evidence: dashboard.html and dashboard.json (each commitment carries cited and, when derived, derivation); trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R6

capabilities.name: Smart Daily Digest
capabilities.claim: Produces a one-screen digest: what needs Sam today, what can wait, and what was auto-archived (aggregated by category, not individually).
capabilities.observable: Prints three sections. 'Needs you today' contains the investor intro m010, the legal signature m018, and press m046; 'Auto-archived' lists categories by count (notification/receipt/newsletter/human_conversation).

capabilities.name: Long Thread Resolution
capabilities.claim: Collapses each long multi-participant thread into participants + milestones + open items, grounded with per-line message-id citations.
capabilities.observable: For t-launch (9 messages, 4 participants) and t-api (4 messages) it prints every milestone by id and the open items (e.g. t-launch open item = m030 pricing approval).

capabilities.name: Relationship Intelligence
capabilities.claim: Builds a per-correspondent profile (relationship type, message volume, and who has been waiting longest on Sam) ranked by the age in days of each sender's oldest unanswered message, not by how many are outstanding.
capabilities.observable: Prints the clock it uses (newest message in the mailbox, 2026-09-09T17:17:00) and a table of the 18 senders with something outstanding, ordered by wait: devika@paperjet.io 6.1d (m008), alerts@sentry.io 5.2d (m090), priya@paperjet.io 4.3d (m030), aria.f@northwind.vc 2.4d (m010). priya has more outstanding messages than devika and still ranks below her.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl events tagged cap=X3 (longest_waits with per-sender waiting_days)

capabilities.name: Autonomous Assistant Planning
capabilities.claim: Produces a prioritized day plan from decisions + commitment dates and, for each row, states what R3's own send-selection policy would do with it. The plan is a view: X4 itself performs no action and writes nothing.
capabilities.observable: Prints 21 ordered plan items (escalations first, then replies by commitment date). Each row's 'next step' is computed by calling R3's selection policy: 'R3 proposes send (needs approval)', 'human decision required', or 'human must author the reply (nothing grounded to send)' (m042). Ends with '8 of 21 plan items would be selected by R3's send policy'.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl events tagged cap=X4 (plan event listing the gateable ids)

capabilities.name: Preference-Aware Negotiation Agent
capabilities.claim: Scans every parsed commitment against the stored cutoff — no message id or time is written into the capability — drafts counter-proposals only where a human is actually waiting on an answer, invents no availability, and hands every draft to R3's gate rather than acting on it.
capabilities.observable: Prints the rule in effect with the sentence it was learned from (m041), finds 3 violations, drafts a counter-proposal only for m043 (monday 9:00am < 11:00am) quoting m041, and marks m038 and m080 'advisory, no draft' because nobody is waiting on an answer. Conflict notices for [m010,m061] and [m013,m016] state that no alternative availability is grounded in the inbox. All 3 drafts are passed to ApprovalGate and come back 'dry_run_would_do'; 'outbox/ writes from X5: 0'.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl events tagged cap=X5 (each draft event records the gate's verdict); memory/preferences.json
